objective: Compare post-mastery retention of independently reviewed component identities under stable component-color exposure and a plain control.

hypotheses.statement: Stable component-identity color introduced after learning criterion may alter delayed, unaided component-identity recognition relative to matched plain-text practice.
Stable color present during initial study may affect acquisition or later retention differently from color introduced only after mastery.

prospectiveProcedure: Construct matched item sets only from independently reviewed source-geometry ownership and unambiguous target component identities.
Randomize target-to-arm assignments within each participant and counterbalance assignment across participants before exposure.
Apply an identical explicit learning criterion to all conditions before the consolidation window.
Equalize post-criterion exposure time and task feedback; introduce stable color only in the assigned arms.
Measure unaided plain-format recognition at preregistered delayed intervals, without the identifying colors.
Score trial responses from fixed source identity keys with assessor-blind condition labels and document attrition.

primary.statistic: within-participant accuracy difference by assigned item set

secondary: response latency on delayed color-free prompts
correct transfer to independently reviewed unfamiliar character arrangements
nonclaims: No participant performance or retention result
No general Mandarin semantic mastery claim

note: A machine-readable design is not a conducted or statistically powered study. Do not infer evidence of educational benefit from implementation or control-arm assignment.
